thread.title: 7 Key Ways To Play Chip Stocks As Micron Soars Again

author: NANCY GONDO
title: 7 Key Ways To Play Chip Stocks As Micron Soars Again
text:
Semiconductors were among sector funds that advanced Tuesday as Micron Technology surged for its second straight day of big gains.
X VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ( SMH ) and iShares PHLX Semiconductor ( SOXX ) rose a respective 0.7% and 0.6% Tuesday. Micron closed with a 6.4% gain as it approaches a 63.52 buy point of a cup base. Shares rose 4% Monday after the data storage maker announced a $10 billion buyback program and raised current-quarter guidance above views. Micron owns high IBD ratings: 95 Composite, 95 Relative Price Strength, 92 Earnings Per Share.
SMH and SOXX have been sticking close to their respective 50-day lines as they work on the right side of bases. The chip sector had come under some recent pressure amid concerns about weak smartphone chip sales. For instance, Apple ( AAPL ) chip supplier Broadcom ( AVGO ) last month lowered the top end of its current-quarter sales outlook. Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) also recently cited weak smartphone sales.
The two largest semiconductor ETFs in terms of assets are $1.7 billion SOXX and $913.4 million SMH. SOXX, which tracks the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index, will turn 17 years old in July. Micron, a top 10 holding, represented a 4.4% weighting in its 30-stock portfolio. Six-year-old SMH tracks the MVIS U.S. Listed Semiconductor 25 Index. Micron was the third-largest holding in SMH as of May 21, with a 5.4% weighting. Its top two positions were Intel and Taiwan Semiconductor.

The ETF's 8.8% year-to-date return through Monday, according to Morningstar Inc., was well ahead of the S&P 500's 3% advance.
Chips have trended higher over the past two years before stalling in late November. SOXX's average annual returns over the past three, five and 10 years of 25.2%, 25.3% and 14%, respectively, outpaced the S&P 500's 10.9%, 12.7% and 9.3% gains. SMH delivered 24.2% over the past three and five years.
More Chips? Other unleveraged semiconductor ETFs include PowerShares Dynamic Semiconductor ( PSI ) with $338.5 million in assets and SPDR S&P Semiconductor ( XSD ) with $328.5 million.
Below are a few ideas for those who prefer leveraged plays, which target double or triple the performance or inverse performance of the underlying index. Be aware that these tend to be more volatile than their nonleveraged counterparts and usually have higher expense ratios.
Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3x Shares ( SOXL ), with $821 million in assets, seeks triple the return of the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index. ProShares Ultra Semiconductors ( USD ) ($81.3 million) aims for two times the daily performance of the Dow Jones U.S. Semiconductors Index.
